did_you_know.text: Psalm 100 opens with the heading “A Psalm for Thanksgiving,” so the theme of gratitude appears from the very beginning.
The call “Make a joyful noise to the LORD” is addressed to “all the earth,” not just to a particular group.
The verse describes three ways of approaching the LORD: serving Him with gladness, coming before Him with joyful singing, and making a joyful sound before Him.
The verse calls us to recognize that the LORD is God, that He made us, and that we are His people and the sheep of His pasture.
The image “the sheep of His pasture” portrays the people as a flock provided for and watched over, expressing belonging and care.
The verse mentions His “gates” and “courts,” together with thanksgiving, praise, giving thanks, and blessing His name; thus, it describes an entrance accompanied by gratitude and praise.
The commands “Give thanks to Him” and “bless His name” emphasize that the gratitude is directed to the LORD and that His name is at the center of the praise.
The conclusion gives the reason for the call to give thanks: “For the LORD is good,” meaning that His goodness is the foundation of gratitude.
The verse presents two dimensions of constancy: the LORD’s steadfast love endures “forever,” and His faithfulness continues “from generation to generation.”
